title: Combined whole-book source and page-projection limits
question: Can the combined recognition and Standard product publish one native whole-book source and project located text across the full page inventory?
method: Publish the combined native product using the exact Standard source and retained managed recognition responses. Adopt the published product after the first annotation attempt encountered a runtime pin mismatch. Finalize the adopted cut, census exact native and directly projected page coverage, and inspect the native and projection pointers on the three pages without a direct join.
commands: uv run python docs/design_review/evidence/2026-11-08_nce-full-book/intake.py build/nce-full-book --release release:845ac25166e63bae9177a19771fece4324453204a080fded91921eec5135e7e1 --realization nce-gs518-source-integrated-adopted --integrated-product 1389 integrated a491d3ddbf3ee964a8a95e6fc6bed59648fb5c5a77bc57cb84411a9205a749f2
uv run ci run finalize 312 --output-realization nce-gs518-integrated-source-result:312 --json

outputs.role: Exact native page, direct projection and annotation inventory
Native and projected inline locator census for pages 4, 119 and 506

results.name: Pages with directly located native projection pieces
results.note: Projected inline text on pages 4 and 119 has regions on the containing nodes.

conclusion: Run 312/cut 431 finalized the adopted combined product and its 29 annotated views without fresh recognition or reconciliation. All 518 pages have native regions. Pages 4 and 119 have projected inline children whose regions reside on their containers. Page 506 retains a selected page header and no body projection. Direct page locators and the effect of replacement on source coverage remain assessment findings.
